sentences.text: In 1883, French engineer Léon Charles Thévenin proved that any linear two-terminal circuit of resistors and sources can be replaced by an equivalent circuit consisting of a single voltage source V_Th in series with a resistor R_Th.
Similarly, Norton's theorem proves the same network can be replaced by an equivalent current source I_N in parallel with a resistor R_N.
V_Th is the open-circuit voltage across terminals a-b. I_N is the short-circuit current flowing when a-b are connected.
The equivalent resistance is R_Th = V_oc / I_sc.
When connecting a load resistor R_L to a practical power source with internal resistance R_Th, how do you maximize the power delivered to the load?
Maximum power transfer occurs when the load resistance exactly equals the Thevenin resistance: R_L = R_Th.
The maximum power delivered is: P_max = V_Th² / (4 R_Th).
